title: Qwen3-VL grounding accuracy degrades in vLLM 0.11.1 and later
body: I am seeing a grounding accuracy issue with Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct on vLLM versions starting with v0.11.1. Bounding-box grounding results are inaccurate compared with the expected locations. My server uses Ubuntu 22.04, PyTorch 2.9.0+cu129, Python 3.12, and eight NVIDIA H20 GPUs. I attached examples of the grounding output.

symptoms_visible: Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Instruct returns grounding boxes at the wrong locations on vLLM 0.11.1 and later.
N0.label: N0 grounding degradation reported

symptoms_visible: The grounding boxes remain inaccurate on the H20 server with the default Flash Attention backend.
Comparable tests on H100, H200, and H20 show misplaced grounding on vLLM 0.11.1 or 0.11.2, while an A100 test and vLLM 0.11.0 produce boxes near the requested object.
N1.label: N1 backend and hardware scope collected

symptoms_visible: The same misplaced grounding result appears with TORCH_SDPA selected for the multimodal encoder.
The same misplaced grounding result appears when the 30B model is run on one H100 with tensor parallel size 1.
N2.label: N2 encoder backend and tensor parallel probes completed

symptoms_visible: With --enforce-eager, the grounding locations are correct on both vLLM 0.11.1 and 0.11.2.
With the normal compiled execution path, the grounding locations are wrong; using --enforce-eager makes inference significantly slower.
N3.label: N3 eager execution isolates compiled path

symptoms_visible: The same grounding test returns accurate locations after using Triton 3.4.0 or rebuilding Triton 3.5 with pull request 9035 cherry-picked.
N4.label: N4 corrected Triton build verified

symptoms_visible: Qwen3-VL returns grounding coordinates at the expected image locations with compiled vLLM execution after installing a Triton build containing the correction.
N_terminal.label: terminal grounding accuracy restored

question_patterns: Which attention backend does the startup log say is being used?
Can you paste the attention-backend line from server startup?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My startup log says that I am using the Flash Attention backend on the V1 engine.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My startup log says I am using a custom attention backend, and switching back to the default fixes the boxes.
The startup line is `Using FLASH_ATTN backend` rather than spelling it as Flash Attention.

question_patterns: Can you confirm the GPU architecture and compare the result on another GPU or vLLM version?
Does the degradation reproduce on Hopper devices, and do you have a working comparison?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I am using 8 H20 Hopper GPUs and see the degradation. In our combined tests, vLLM 0.11.1 or 0.11.2 gives misplaced boxes on H20, H100, and H200, while the A100 result remains accurate. We also compared 0.11.2 with 0.11.0 using the same Wikipedia login-button query.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The boxes are equally inaccurate on A100 and H20, including with vLLM 0.11.0.
The same version comparison was run on H100 rather than H20, with the same bad and good outputs.

edges.comment: Real thread c0-c10. Reports from H100, H200, and A100 users are folded into the simulated user side. The answers contain observed startup output and hardware/version comparisons, not a conclusion about the defective component.

question_patterns: Please launch with --mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA and report whether the grounding output changes.
Can you test TORCH_SDPA for the multimodal encoder to distinguish the encoder path from the language-model path?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I launched with `--mm-encoder-attn-backend TORCH_SDPA`. There was no change; the result was the same as before.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: TORCH_SDPA makes the grounding boxes accurate again.

question_patterns: Can you repeat the test without tensor parallelism?
Please run the smaller Qwen3-VL model on one GPU with tensor parallel size 1 and report the grounding result.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking on one H100 with `--tensor-parallel-size 1 --pipeline-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 50000`. The grounding result was still the same.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The single-GPU TP=1 run is accurate, and the boxes become wrong only with tensor parallelism.

edges.comment: Real thread c12-c14. These are configuration probes, so they are clarification-only measurements. Their raw result rules out simple encoder-backend and tensor-parallel explanations without putting an engineer diagnosis in the user's answer.

question_patterns: Can you add --enforce-eager and rerun the same grounding example?
Please compare the grounding output with eager execution enabled.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Adding `--enforce-eager` restores the grounding result for qwen3-vl-235b-a22b-instruct-fp8 on both vLLM 0.11.1 and 0.11.2. I included my deployment parameters and additional output examples. It also makes inference significantly slower.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Eager execution restores accuracy on 0.11.2, but I did not repeat the test on 0.11.1.

edges.comment: Real thread c15-c20, with multiple affected users folded together. This is a handler-requested execution-mode probe. The reporter observed that eager execution restores coordinates and reduces speed; attributing that contrast to TorchInductor/Triton rather than CUDA-graph capture is engineer-side reasoning reserved for the final solution.

question_patterns: Can you test Triton 3.4.0 or rebuild Triton 3.5 with triton-lang/triton pull request 9035 cherry-picked, then rerun the grounding example?
Please try the corrected Triton build and report only whether the same grounding benchmark recovers.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the alternatives. Downgrading Triton from 3.5.0 to 3.4.0 restored accuracy. Rebuilding Triton 3.5 with triton-lang/triton PR 9035 cherry-picked also fixed the grounding output; this was confirmed with vLLM 0.13.0 and 0.14.0 images.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Neither Triton 3.4.0 nor the Triton 3.5 build with PR 9035 changes the misplaced coordinates.
Only the patched Triton 3.5 build was tested, and it restored accuracy.

edges.comment: Real thread c25-c35. Results from affected users who tested the downgrade and cherry-picked build are folded into one user side. This is pre-resolution candidate-build verification and therefore remains a clarification-only measurement.

solution.intent: Replace the buggy TorchInductor/Triton compiled-kernel path with a Triton build containing the compiler correction, while retaining compiled vLLM execution, and have the user rerun the grounding benchmark before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: The degradation is caused by the TorchInductor/Triton-generated kernels used by the compiled language-model path, not by Flash Attention or CUDA-graph capture itself. Install Triton 3.4.0, or preferably a compatible Triton build containing triton-lang/triton PR 9035, restart vLLM without relying on full `--enforce-eager`, and rerun the same fixed-image grounding test to verify that its coordinates match the expected boxes.
solution.inference_hint: The user only observed backend logs and the outcomes of SDPA, TP=1, eager-mode, and Triton-version tests. Engineers concluded that Triton is involved through TorchInductor/torch.compile and that the faulty generated kernels—not Flash Attention and not CUDA-graph capture itself—cause the coordinate corruption. The restoration with Triton 3.4 or PR 9035 is the evidence supporting that inference.

edges.comment: Technical resolution from c22-c44: the issue was traced to the PyTorch/TorchInductor and Triton compiler combination, with triton-lang/triton PR 9035 correcting the behavior. Full eager mode is a diagnostic workaround but carries a substantial speed penalty. Release scheduling and dependency-rollout reversals are deliberately not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause as incorrect kernels generated through the TorchInductor/torch.compile Triton path, associated with the affected Triton compiler behavior corrected by triton-lang/triton PR 9035.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected contrasts: TORCH_SDPA for the multimodal encoder and TP=1 do not change the output, eager execution restores accuracy, and Triton 3.4 or a PR-9035-patched Triton build restores accuracy.
Must not blame Flash Attention, the multimodal encoder backend, tensor parallelism, or CUDA-graph capture itself as the final cause; the in-case probes do not support those directions.

Must recommend a corrected Triton runtime, such as Triton 3.4.0 or a compatible build containing PR 9035, rather than treating full --enforce-eager as the preferred permanent solution because eager execution significantly reduces inference speed.
Must ask the user to rerun the same grounding example or benchmark on a runtime containing the correction and confirm accurate coordinates before treating the issue as resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced ML inference operator who can deploy very large multimodal models across eight GPUs, alter vLLM launch flags, compare runtime versions, install custom dependencies, and run controlled grounding tests.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and technically detailed; supplies launch commands and visual examples, confirms requested probes directly, and highlights operational tradeoffs such as the inference-speed penalty of eager execution.
